If we look at the last paragraph of the minutes, we can see that at the end of the meeting, the conclusion about all of the activities of the HVO were issued. Do you recall these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended the meeting, and I can confirm that these minutes do indeed come from that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the government making a conclusion calling upon the chief of the Main Staff to come and report on the military and security situation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this occurred at this very meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have time left for the next minutes, unless we don't have that time, I can continue tomorrow. Thank you. Mr. President, I only have one request of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it is better to reconvene tomorrow. We still have 30 seconds left today. It is better to resume the hearing tomorrow. Mr. Alaburic, you wanted to put a final question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I fully understand and agree that we should continue tomorrow. However, I should like the witness to be allowed to take the documents I prepared along with him, because we will be working on them tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to that, Mr. President. This is cross-examination, and I think that the manner in which this examination and the others are being led is such that it's not appropriate for witnesses to be sent home with documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will consult my fellow Judges on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before you decide on the matter, let me just tell you that one protected witness, whose name I therefore cannot utter in the courtroom, and who is very important for my client, was able to take along all the documents prepared for him by the Defence for Mr. Petkovic. We were all in agreement about it. We wanted him to be fully familiar with the documents we would be discussing the following day. Nobody opposed that, and this was the basis on which we proceeded in our cross-examination. This was a Prosecution witness who was heard in the month of November of last year. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all, you know, this is yet another surprise. No one raised this with the Prosecution previously, so this is completely coming to us from out of the blue, as we say. I don't know about prior precedent. I don't know about other witnesses. What I know is that this is not appropriate to raise at the very end of the day, when a stack of papers has been dropped on the Prosecution at about the same moment it's being dropped on the witness. If we're going to establish a precedent of sending all the witnesses back to their hotels with the documents, it's something that could have been done much more frequently or in earlier stages of the trial. There certainly could have been times when the Prosecution could have availed itself of a procedure. But to raise it now and, frankly, to not extend the courtesy of at least giving the Prosecution some advance notice of their intention to make this request, we oppose it. This is not how this trial has been run. It hasn't been run in this way in the last year, and we oppose it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What did you want to say, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session for a moment, and I will give you the full name of the witness. Therefore, it will become obvious that this was not a precedent, my proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session. One moment. This is about a protected witness. In other words, the witness should not be aware -- made aware of the name of this witness. That's a problem. Well, we know there's a protected witness. No need to give his name. The Judges are going to discuss it straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I should mention that on record we are now in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, the Trial Chamber reminds Ms. Alaburic that she should have warned us of this, at least at the beginning of the hearing, and not at 1915, which forces the interpreters to work an extra 15 minutes, and we are very sorry to have been faced with this issue at this time of the day. The Trial Chamber also deems that most of the documents can be broken down into two main parts. There are texts that the witness is supposed to know and meetings which he attended. As such, there is no particular reason why he should not be allowed to see the documents, be it only to refresh his memory or for him to be more efficient. This decision is not going to be a precedent. Of course, this is a decision on a case-by-case basis. The Trial Chamber is therefore going to ask the usher or the Registrar to give the binder to the witness so that he can inspect it tonight and tomorrow morning, since we're going to reconvene tomorrow at 2.15. The hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of July, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
